title: King of Zugzwang
summary: Use a queen sacrifice to reach the right rook ending, then avoid stalemate and defeat a checking knight promotion.

nodes.question: How can White answer the mating threat on c2?
nodes.explanation: White has Kc1, Rd1 and Qf8 against Ka1, Rg2, a4 and b3. The queen can force the rook onto a2 before Rd2 prepares the needed recapture.

branches.title: Prepare the recapture and solve the rook ending
commentary: Begin from the complete seven-piece source board. The later rook ending is part of the checked line, rather than an assumed conversion.
Qa3+ forces a response while aligning the black rook with the queen.
Ra2 is the only legal reply to the queen check.
Rd2 prepares to recapture on b2 if Black checks with the pawn, while offering the queen on a3.
b2+ is the illustrated countercheck, trying to exploit White’s exposed king.
Qxb2+ removes the checking pawn and offers the queen with check.
Rxb2 captures the queen, but the rook has now been drawn onto the prepared second rank.
Rxb2 recaptures. White has a winning rook against the a-pawn, but must still avoid stalemate.
a3 pushes toward promotion and creates the source’s next stalemate problem.
Rb1+ checks along the first rank, forcing the king to step in front of its own pawn.
Ka2 blocks a3 from advancing for a move.
Rb4 takes the fourth rank and confines the king.
Ka1 is the only legal move, returning behind the pawn.
Kc2 improves the king while allowing the a-pawn to advance.
a2 advances, threatening promotion once Ka1 clears the square.
Kb3 approaches the pawn without stalemating Black.
Kb1 clears a1 and threatens promotion on the next move.
Rh4 prepares to answer a queen promotion by mating on the first rank.
a1=N+ underpromotes with check, avoiding that immediate queen-promotion mate.
Kc3 answers the knight check and keeps control of b2 and c2.
Ka2 is the source’s selected escape attempt with the king.
Rh8 waits while preparing a-file and second-rank mating threats.
Kb1 returns toward the corner; the knight cannot supply a useful escape for its king.
Rh2 takes the second rank, leaving Black to move in the mating net.
Kc1 is the selected final king move, walking onto the first-rank mate.
Rh1# is actual mate. Kc3 covers b2, c2 and d2, the rook covers the first rank, and Na1 cannot block the checking line.
branches.explanation: Rh1# is actual mate. Kc3 covers b2, c2 and d2, the rook covers the first rank, and Na1 cannot block the checking line.

branches.title: Accept the offered queen immediately
commentary: Compare the source’s direct acceptance of the queen offered by Rd2.
Qa3+ checks from the a-file.
Ra2 is forced to stop the check.
Rd2 offers the queen and prepares the rook’s lateral switch.
Rxa3 takes the queen, but leaves Black’s own pieces obstructing one another.
Rb2 blocks the b-pawn and confines Ka1 behind the a-rook.
Ra2 is the only legal move: a4 is blocked by Ra3, b3 by Rb2, and the king has no safe square.
Rb1# is actual mate. Kc1 protects the rook on b1, and Black’s own rook and pawns close the remaining flights.
branches.explanation: Rb1# is actual mate. Kc1 protects the rook on b1, and Black’s own rook and pawns close the remaining flights.

branches.title: Check without preparing Rd2
commentary: Compare the source’s natural queen check before the white rook reaches the second rank.
Qf6+ gives away the forced win by allowing a pawn countercheck.
b2+ checks while blocking the queen’s diagonal attack on Ka1.
Qxb2+ removes the pawn and gives check, but White’s rook is still on d1.
Rxb2 takes the queen. White cannot recapture from d1; the exact resulting rook ending is drawn.
branches.explanation: Rxb2 takes the queen. White cannot recapture from d1; the exact resulting rook ending is drawn.

exercises.answer: It puts the rook on the rank where it can recapture after ...b2+ Qxb2+ ...Rxb2. With the rook on d1, the same exchange leaves Black’s rook alive.

exercises.prompt: Why is winning the black rook not the end of the lesson?
exercises.answer: The a-pawn can create stalemate and checking underpromotion resources. White must coordinate king and rook before claiming a completed win.

startContext: The complete seven-piece source root is visually reconstructed. Selected source branches cover the queen offer, the prepared b2 recapture, rook maneuvering against the a-pawn and the checking knight underpromotion, ending in actual mate. The drawn Qf6+ comparison is checked independently of the source’s verbal assessment; the selected king replies do not constitute an exhaustive defense tree.
verification_scope: Saved board images reviewed manually. Every encoded intermediate position and endpoint is checked against the tablebase. Selected instructive variations, not an exhaustive tree of all legal defenses.
